home.title: A gate between your AI agent and your money.
home.sub: A NEAR smart contract. Your agent can pay only for the jobs you signed off. Everything else is refused, and the refusal is recorded on-chain.
home.s1: An AI agent wants to spend your money.
home.s2: You stamp (sign) each job it may pay for: who gets paid, how much, and the exact instruction.
home.s3: The agent asks for exactly that job, within your limit: paid.
home.s4: A different instruction, a fake owner, or a higher amount: refused, and recorded.
home.s5: Above the review amount you set, a payment waits for your approval.
home.ctaConsoleHelp: For owners. Needs a NEAR testnet wallet.
home.ctaProofHelp: Real transactions you can check yourself.
home.linkTry: Try to break it with your own wallet
home.linkTryHelp: Safe: it only sends requests the gate refuses. Testnet only.
home.paidBody: Testnet NEAR leaves the gate's escrow only for a stamped job.
home.heldBody: Above your review amount, the payment waits up to one hour for your approval.
home.refusedBody: Nothing is paid. The reason is saved on the public ledger, so anyone can check what the agent tried.
home.evidence: 10 scene transactions are recorded on the proof page: 2 payments, 2 settled approvals, 1 hold, and 5 refusals or failures. Each hash is on the public testnet explorer.
home.limitsBody: This is a testnet prototype. It is not audited. Mainnet is not deployed. The wallet list has 6 wallets. Signing in the wallet window was tested with Intear. Meteor was checked up to the mainnet-account notice. Creating a gate locks NEAR in that account, and the gate cannot be deleted. The stamp key cannot be replaced. Anyone who knows a live mandate serial can freeze it. Nothing is paid. Issue a new mandate to recover. The old serial stays frozen, and the new one can be frozen the same way. The refusal count goes back to 0 only when a request passes the mandate checks with an amount above 0 and the transaction does not fail, whatever follows: a payment, a new hold, a spend-rule refusal (tier2_deny), or an allowed request that pays nothing (an authorize call or an action other than a transfer). A zero-amount request leaves the count unchanged. Approving or rejecting a hold later does not change it. Anyone can grow the gate's storage with refused requests. That can block a full withdrawal until a plain NEAR transfer to the gate account, not Deposit, covers the shortfall. In the sandbox, 3 requests grew storage by 63,758 bytes and a full withdrawal failed with LackBalanceForState, about 0.028 NEAR short. The contract has no per-mandate storage cap. The fix is designed, not deployed.

man.freeze: The refusal count goes back to 0 only when a request passes the mandate checks with an amount above 0 and the transaction does not fail, whatever follows: a payment, a new hold, a spend-rule refusal (tier2_deny), or an allowed request that pays nothing (an authorize call or an action other than a transfer). A zero-amount request leaves the count unchanged. Approving or rejecting a hold later does not change it. A spend-rule refusal still uses the job and its share of the budget, and nothing is paid.
man.limitFreeze: Anyone who knows a mandate serial can freeze it with the same refused request from the same account twice in a row (with no passing request in between), or three mandate-check refusals in a row. Nothing is paid. A new mandate recovers use, and that mandate can be frozen again.
man.limitStorage: Anyone can grow the gate's storage with refused requests that carry long strings: in the sandbox, 3 requests grew storage by 63,758 bytes, and a full escrow withdrawal then failed with LackBalanceForState, about 0.028 NEAR short. A plain NEAR transfer (not Deposit) of the shortfall fixes it. There is no per-mandate storage cap in the contract (a 4th call on an already frozen mandate added 0 bytes in that run), and the fix is designed, not deployed.
man.spare: Anyone who knows a mandate's serial can freeze it. Keep a spare mandate ready.

agent.s1: 2. Issue a mandate and save it
agent.s1body: In the same step, set the budget, the expiry and the jobs, then press Issue mandate. Press Copy mandate JSON and save the text as a .json file in the folder your agent reads mandates from.
agent.s2body: The agent code is in the repository under agent/src, and the setup steps are in agent/README.md. Point the paths at the key file you saved, your mandates folder and a ledger file the agent writes. First run chmod 600 on the key file: the agent refuses a key file that other users can read.
agent.s3body: Call chopgate_status: it lists your stamped jobs, each with an entry_id. Then call chopgate_pay with that entry_id, the amount in NEAR and the source "owner_chat". The gate returns a verdict and a reason code. All parameters are in agent/README.md.
agent.warn: The same refused request from the same account twice in a row (with no passing request in between), or three mandate-check refusals in a row, freeze a mandate. Calls from anyone other than the agent count. Nothing is paid. The refusal count goes back to 0 only when a request passes the mandate checks with an amount above 0 and the transaction does not fail, whatever follows: a payment, a new hold, a spend-rule refusal (tier2_deny), or an allowed request that pays nothing (an authorize call or an action other than a transfer). A zero-amount request leaves the count unchanged. Approving or rejecting a hold later does not change it.

agent.s0body: In the console, open Mandates, type an agent name and press Create agent account. Your wallet creates a sub-account, sends it 1 testnet NEAR for gas and adds one key. That key can call a single method, authorize_and_pay_tiered, on your gate. It cannot transfer NEAR. Press Save file to keep chopgate-agent-key.json: the console shows this key only once.
